idiom_name: framework-independent screen-state class plus view projection with explicit or bound synchronization
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give each screen one plain object that owns the dynamic state, the derived display decisions and the command handlers, with no widget or toolkit types; let the view read it and forward user gestures back. Derive control state through named read-only properties so the rule lives in the model, and keep business rules in domain objects the model reads. Keep the two sides consistent through the platform's binding facility where one exists, otherwise through a coarse-grained save/reload step or a small observer list; decide explicitly where that synchronization code lives (view, model or mapper) because that decision determines what the tests can reach. Where the model must observe the view (Fowler's 'model references view' shape), depend on a narrow view interface so tests can substitute a stub.
code_sketch:
class AlbumPresentationModel:
    def __init__(self, albums): ...          # domain data injected
    @property
    def composer_enabled(self):               # display decision
        return self.is_classical
    def apply(self): ...                      # command

# view: bind widgets to model properties and call its commands
composer_entry.enabled = model.composer_enabled
pitfalls: Letting the model hold or manipulate widgets: the logic is no longer testable without a UI.
Leaving the placement of the synchronization code unspecified, so both sides assume the other reloads.
Growing one screen-wide object instead of one presentation model per view or child control.

Wrong move: make both the View and Presentation Model authoritative for the same mutable field -> Y fails because two-way notifications can oscillate or overwrite newer edits -> instead Z choose one owner for each state value and make the other side a projection or explicit mapper.

Wrong move: leave observers or bindings attached after the View is destroyed -> Y fails because callbacks retain dead views or update half-torn-down widgets -> instead Z detach subscriptions at teardown or use lifecycle-aware or weak bindings.
